ordered_diagnoses: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation

s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with bilateral testicular enlargement
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes on scrotal ultrasound
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
key_facts: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
Bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Left radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed
Tumor size: 7.0 × 6.0 × 4.2 cm
Histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types

shortlist: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with three distinct cell types, consistent with non-seminomatous germ cell tumor

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with small, medium, and large cells, a characteristic feature of embryonal carcinoma

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral testicular enlargement and large solid masses, although less likely given the pleomorphic histology

shortlist.label: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of three distinct cell types, which could represent somatic differentiation within a germ cell tumor

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types, which could be consistent with a teratoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor with three distinct cell types and the lack of elevated serum tumor markers are consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, which can have a variety of histologic patterns and may not always have elevated tumor markers.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas typically have a more uniform cell population and often present with elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: While embryonal carcinoma is a type of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, it typically has a more aggressive clinical course and may present with elevated α-fetoprotein levels, which were not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation
rejected.why: This diagnosis would require evidence of somatic differentiation, such as the presence of teratomatous elements, which were not described in the histologic examination.

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are a type of germ cell tumor that contain several different types of tissues, but the histologic examination in this case described a pleomorphic tumor with three distinct cell types, which is more consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor.
